newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian SIDANKO to unveil strategic partner - source.
newsitem.headline: Russian SIDANKO to unveil strategic partner - source.

text.p: Russian oil major SIDANKO will soon announce a strategic partnership with a major international energy company, sources close to the project said on Friday.
The officials declined to name the partner, said by the Sevodnya daily newspaper on Friday to be Shell, the U.S. unit of Royal Dutch/Shell Group, Mobil Corp or an Iranian-Arab concern.
A Shell spokeswoman and a Mobil source declined to comment.

But the sources, who work closely with SIDANKO, said Russia's fourth-largest oil producer would soon announce the name of its partner and a long-term project to tap new reserves, rehabilitate existing wells and upgrade infrastructure.

Oleg Sapozhnikov, spokesman of MFK, the Moscow bank which is a financial consultant to SIDANKO, said a well-known foreign oil company stood behind an unknown offshore company which recently granted SIDANKO a loan collateralised by SIDANKO shares.
"The name behind Kantupun is a very well known oil company; a serious, strategic partner," Sapozhnikov said.
Cyrpus-registered Kantupun Holding Company Ltd granted a loan to SIDANKO under a December 1996 deal collateralised by a 34 percent SIDANKO stake controlled by Interros-Oil.
Interros-Oil won the stake in an investment tender in September 1996. It also has a 51 percent stake in SIDANKO acquired through a tender in January.
MFK is associated with Uneximbank, the lynchpin of the Interros financial-industrial group which includes Interros-Oil.
"Kantupun is an offshore company behind which stands a major investor that is a major force in the international energy world," said Sergei Chernitsyn of Uneximbank.

OAO Sibirsko-Dalnevostochnaya Neftyanyaya Kompaniya (SIDANKO), a vertically-integrated oil company, has the Chernogorneft CHGZ.RTS, Kondpetroleum COND.RTS and Varyoganneftegaz VJGZ.RTS crude oil production units. It accounts for around eight percent of total Russian oil output.

SIDANKO said last year that it planned to issue convertible bonds and to treble its authorised capital. SIDANKO also said in February that it was seeking $3 billion in investment in coming years and was talking to major potential investors.
Most of the world's major oil companies have talked to or are in talks with Russian oil companies and analysts have said that strategic partnerships may materialise.
